title: Project communication shared definitions (fabric-project-comms/0.1, DEC-0022 proposed)

projectId.description: A Project's server-issued id. Data, not authority.

opaqueId.description: A thread, message, request, delivery, attempt or cursor id issued by the board.

epoch.description: The namespace epoch the board issued; a retired epoch is refused (idempotency_window_expired).

settledBy.description: Present only when the estate owner settled the request (DEC-0081): a trusted operator principal, the owner of the request's target Project, through com.reconcile of an outcome_unknown request while no responder held the slot. A board sends it on every owner settlement and on nothing else, so its absence means the responder settled the request (com.complete or com.reconcile), and a reader is told the owner, not the responder, attested the outcome.

provenance.description: trusted: the board verified the principal (managed session, enrollment); asserted: the principal said so.

text.description: At most 65536 UTF-8 bytes; the board refuses a larger body before hashing or storing it.

findingSeverity.description: How much the finding matters to what it affects, as its sender judges it (DEC-0080). It is descriptive: its effect on notifications, the Telegram mirror or holds is not decided here.

repositoryName.description: A repository as <owner>/<name>, the path of the canonical GitHub URL a backlog source manifest names (https://github.com/<owner>/<name>): an owner of 1 to 39 letters, digits and hyphens that starts with a letter or digit, and a name of 1 to 100 of [A-Za-z0-9._-] that is not . or .. and has at most one leading dot (.github). Compared as written (DEC-0080).

repositoryPath.description: A file path relative to the repository's root: segments of [A-Za-z0-9._-] joined by single slashes, no leading or trailing slash, and no segment that starts with a dot, so no ., .. or hidden segment (DEC-0080).

backlogRowId.description: A backlog row's stable id, unique within its source file. The knowledge base's backlog contract (fabric-workspace knowledge/backlog.md) requires a nonempty string id; this pattern deliberately narrows it to 1 to 64 of [A-Za-z0-9._-] starting with a letter or digit, so no id holds a space, a colon or a slash. Compared as written (DEC-0080).

dedupeKey.description: The sender's name for what a finding is about: the same sender Project and dedupeKey answer the retained finding's receipt with repeated: true and store no message (DEC-0080). Compared as written.

hostTaskId.description: A task of the host that serves the board: the issuing host's task, in the grammar of a delegation token's task (DEC-0041, delegation-token.schema.json#/$defs/task), issued by the host, not by the board. Opaque, so compared as written (DEC-0076's opaque ids).

affectedRow.description: A backlog row, named by repository, path and id: the row's identity in the common backlog. It links to the row and never copies it.

affectedTask.description: A task of the host that serves the board, named by its id (hostTaskId, DEC-0041's task). It links to the task and never copies it.

affectedRedacted.description: What a reader sees in place of an affects item outside its grants: the item's place and the count stay, what it names does not. Only in a message as read, never in com.submit.

finding.description: A structured finding (DEC-0080): only on a message of kind finding. Evidence is the message's artifacts; there is no evidence member. comms-submit adds that its affects items are distinct and never redacted; in a message as read an item outside the reader's grants is {redacted: true}, in its place, and FAC-SEM-108 refuses two unredacted items that are the same.

consequence.description: What happens to what it affects if nobody acts, 1 to 500 characters.

affects.description: What the finding affects, 1 to 16 items.
